content.title: NCAA Wrestling Championships, 2026: Complete 285-pound bracket
content.text: Rutgers SportsUpdated: Mar. 21, 2026, 10:57 p.m.Published: Mar. 18, 2026, 6:10 p.m.Virginia Tech’s Jimmy Mullen (left) lost a 12-1 major decision to Nick Feldman of Ohio State in a 285-pound consolation round bout at the NCAA wrestling national championships, Friday, March 21, 2025, in Philadelphia. Mullen is from Kearny and is a 3-time New Jersey state champion for St. Joseph (Mont.).Andrew Mills | NJ Advance Media for NJ.comAt last year’s NCAA Wrestling Championships, it was the heavyweight match that stole the show.Oklahoma State’s Wyatt Hendrickson stunned Minnesota’s Gable Steveson, a two-time national champion and Olympic gold medalist, with a takedown in the last 20 seconds of the final.Watch MoreThe heavyweights this year will be hard-pressed to match the drama of last year’s tournament.Three wrestlers with New Jersey ties will try to make their mark, though.David Szuba, who transferred from Rider to Arizona State this year, comes in as the No. 10 seed. Three-time state champion and Virginia Tech sophomore Jimmy Mullen is seeded 16th.Rutgers senior Hunter Catka, a former blood rounder at Virginia Tech, will try to take the long road as the No. 27 seed.2026 NCAA Wrestling ChampionshipsWhen: March 19-21Where: Rocket Arena, ClevelandTV: ESPN, ESPN2, ESPNUStreaming: ESPN+Brackets125 | 133 | 141 |149 | 157165 | 174 | 184 | 197 | 285ScheduleThursday, March 19: Session 1 (pigtails and first-round competition), noon (ESPN2 and ESPN+); Session 2 (Second round and wrestleback first round), 7 p.m. (ESPN and ESPN+)Friday, March 20: Session 3 (quarterfinals, wrestleback second and third rounds), noon (ESPNU and ESPN+); Session 4 (Semifinals, blood round and wrestleback fifth round), 8 p.m. (ESPN2 and ESPN+)Saturday, March 21: Session 5 (Wrestleback semifinals and medal rounds), 11 a.m. (ESPNU and ESPN+); Session 6 (National finals), 6:30 p.m. (ESPN and ESPN+)Reigning team champion: Penn StateReturning champions (this year’s weight in parentheses): Vincent Robinson, North Carolina State (125); Lucas Byrd, Illinois (133); **Jesse Mendez, Ohio State (141); Antrell Taylor, Nebraska (157); Mitchell Messenbrink (165); Levi Haines, Penn State (174); AJ Ferrari, Nebraska (285).How to watch Rutgers men’s basketball today against Creighton: FREE live stream for College Basketball Crown Rutgers gymnastics advances in NCAA Championships: Here is who it will face nextGary Redus gets 1st major win at Rutgers, lands top recruit once committed to other Big Ten school Rutgers grad sues school over ‘gross negligence’ in racking up $516 million sports debtDC Travis Johansen is bringing ‘fresh start’ to Rutgers.
